snippet.title: Lullaby Lounge
snippet.description:
Welcome to Lullaby Lounge, your sanctuary for calm historical narratives.

Tired of history documentaries filled with loud music and dramatic reenactments? 

So were we. Our videos explore the fascinating, mundane, and often forgotten details of daily life throughout history, from the Roman Empire to the Victorian Era. Each story is told with a steady, soothing voice and gentle ambient sounds, specifically designed to help you relax, learn, and gently drift off to sleep. 

If you love history but need a quieter way to enjoy it, you're in the right place. At Lullaby Lounge, we create a tranquil atmosphere to help you relax, de-stress, and enjoy restful nights. Subscribe and join us on a journey to better sleep.

snippet.description:
Yore History covers historical documentaries in narrated 3rd person and historical fiction in 2nd person. The 2nd Person content places YOU in the role of various people throughout history in a unique and personal way!

The historical documentary series will cover the rise and fall of empires such as the Achaemenid Persian Empire, Roman Empire, Parthian Empire, Ancient Greece, Mongolian Empire, Chinese Dynasties, ancient Japan and various other empires, kingdoms and regions throughout history.  In addition, it will cover unique battles and moments in  history!

Both types of content while educational have a focus on epic entertainment...history is far from the boring topic some teachers taught...history is our collective past and filled with all kinds of emotions and this channel hopes to capture them!

snippet.title: youdoc
snippet.description:
Docema is a Massachusetts film company that produces historical documentaries enlivened by dramatic narratives and what has become its trademark: extraordinary 3D computer animations.

Docema was founded in 2003 by Bruce Twickler a software industry veteran who published, among other products, VideoWorks in 1985, and, a decade later, VideoCraft, with its 1996 incarnation on the internet as The Amazing Instant Online Animated Banner Maker. At Docema in 2003 we felt that state-of-the-art software running on high-performance personal computers would be able to produce high-resolution animations with startling realism... enough to produce Hollywood special effects on a public television budget.

The first film, Damrell's Fire, recounts the Great Boston Fire of 1872 and how John Damrell, Boston’s fire chief, directed his firefighters to stem the 65-acre fire.

Our second film was Broadside, which centered on the little known but empire-making era of the Anglo-Dutch Wars in the 17th century.

To view the show in full interactive 360, download the Google Spotlight Stories app now.
Don’t forget to wear headphones!

Android: goo.gl/1gE2PR
iOs: goo.gl/2TJm3J

How to watch:
Mobile: Moving your phone around lets you move the camera in the virtual world of the story. 
Google Cardboard: With a Cardboard viewer, touch the device screen and select the cardboard icon in the bottom right. Load the viewer and watch.
Google Daydream: With a Daydream-ready phone, a compatible headset and the Daydream app, download and watch!
YouTube: Look for non-interactive 360 degree videos from our Google Spotlight Stories channel.
VR: Several of our shows are available on Viveport and Steam for full size 6D.

To learn more about Google Spotlight Stories at: https://www.google.com/atap/spotlight-stories/

snippet.title: Scarlet Fields
snippet.description:
This channel explores the rise and fall of empires, the evolution of warfare, and the human cost behind history’s greatest conflicts.

Here, history is not a list of dates — it is the pulse of nations, the echo of drums, the silence after the guns fade. Each episode dives deep into battles, inventions, revolutions, and ideologies that forged the modern world.

Witness the age when kings fell, machines roared, and humanity learned the true meaning of total war.

Welcome to the fields where history bled — and the world was remade.

Witness the age when kings fell, machines roared, and humanity learned the true meaning of total war.

Welcome to the fields where history bled — and the world was remade.

snippet.title: CandleHearth1600s
snippet.description:
Welcome to CandleHearth1600s — a journey back to the world of early America.
Here, history comes alive through faceless storytelling, uncovering what life was really like between 1600–1700.

🔥 What you’ll discover:

Daily Life & Survival — how colonists farmed, hunted, healed, and built their world.

Stories & Characters — settlers, rebels, Native leaders, pirates, and figures from the Salem Witch Trials.

Conflicts & Problems — uprisings, slavery, native resistance, and deadly outbreaks that shaped the colonies.

Culture & Beliefs — religion, superstition, myths, and the traditions that guided everyday life.

Each video is crafted to feel like sitting by a candlelit hearth, listening to the untold stories of a time when survival was uncertain and belief shaped reality.

If you love immersive history, powerful storytelling, and learning how the 1600s shaped America, hit Subscribe and step back in time.

snippet.title: SandRhoman History
snippet.description:
We want to entertain people with history which is entertaining, visually pleasing and grounded in scholarship at the same time.

Our golden rules:
1) We only use academic sources and always try to stick to the consensus opinion.
2) We always list our sources in description of our videos.
3) We make clear when we deviate from the prior two rules.

Education: Between the two of us we hold two Master's degrees in history from the university of Bern and one degree as a history teacher from the Bern University of Teacher Education. Both of us worked at the University of Bern as teaching assistants.

We wrote an article about our experience as content creators (ed. by Dr. Kilian Baur and Robert Trautmannsberger): https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/9783110792898-005/html

We also held a few talks about our journey on YouTube at the universities of Eichstätt, Fribourg and Zürich. 

We taught a seminar about history on YouTube at the University of Zurich in spring of 2024.
